issues.body: `_worker_no_change_pred` returns false when `worker_no_change_rate_1h` is null, while `compute_recoveries` adds a recovery whenever that predicate is false for every row in the recovery window. Thus, after `recover_snapshots` consecutive collected snapshots with an unreadable or otherwise unavailable model-health signal, an existing `worker-no-change` alert is eligible for auto-close despite no numeric evidence that the rate cleared. The new test proves recovery for measured 0.0 snapshots, but it does not start from null-rate snapshots, so this fail-open path remains untested and unchanged.
issues.fix_hint: Give `worker-no-change` a measurable-clear recovery condition: require every recovery-window row to contain a numeric no-change rate (with the required sample semantics) before declaring recovery. Add a non-vacuous assertion that consecutive collected null-rate snapshots do not include `(target, WORKER_NO_CHANGE)` in recoveries, while consecutive measured healthy snapshots still do.
issues.title: Unavailable no-change telemetry is still treated as confirmed recovery

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-5 major finding remains unchanged. The worker-no-change firing predicate correctly treats a null rate as non-firing, but the generic recovery logic still interprets that same false result as confirmed clearance. Therefore, consecutive collected snapshots with unavailable no-change telemetry can auto-close a live worker-no-change alert without measured evidence of recovery. The added recovery assertions cover measured 0.0 snapshots and continued firing only; they do not exercise null-rate recovery. Progress is stagnant because the same fail-open recovery path remains at the same severity.
